# Streaming text

A model’s answer arriving a token at a time, in the reading voice, without layout shift, and announced once when it ends.

Status: Stable. Semantic versioning applies: nothing breaks without a deprecation first.

Text that arrives a token at a time.

- **The reading voice.** A model’s answer is set in Alegreya because it is *read* — several paragraphs, at the reader’s pace. The chrome is Archivo; anything the machine *did* (a tool, an argument, an id) is a Martian Mono literal, because it is *inspected*. A reader can tell from the letterforms alone whether they are looking at the model talking, the model acting, or the product.
- **No layout shift.** Text only grows at its end, and the block caret is a fixed-width inline box after the last glyph, so nothing above it reflows. A block caret reads as *output being written*; a thin bar would read as a field waiting for input.
- **Announced once.** A live region on the text would read every token aloud. Instead the text is `aria-busy` while it streams and a separate polite status says “Response complete.” at the end.
- **Cost grows with the block, not the answer.** Finished blocks are parsed once and kept, and each is a memoised component, so a chunk re-parses and re-renders only the block still arriving. Re-parsing from the top made every token cost the length of the answer before it: in jsdom, 20,000 tokens arriving four at a time took 67 s and rendered finished citations about a million times; now it takes 8 s and about 1,400. Pass `renderCitation` as a stable function, or finished blocks render again.
- **Reduced motion.** The caret stops blinking and stays — still true, since text is still arriving.

## Usage

### When to use

- Rendering an assistant’s answer as it streams, with a block caret at the end.
- Paragraphs, lists, code blocks, inline code and [n] citation markers from a model.
- Text the reader may skim, such as reasoning, with tone set to muted.

### When not to

- An answer in Markdown with headings, tables, numbered lists or links. Use [Markdown](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/ai-markdown--overview.md).
- Long-form markup that does not stream, such as rendered documentation. Use [Prose](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/components-typography-prose--overview.md).
- Text the system says in its own voice, such as labels and hints. Use [Text](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/components-typography-text--overview.md).
- Saying that work is under way before any text exists, outside a message. Use [Run status](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/ai-run-status--overview.md).

### Do and don’t

- Do: Append to text as tokens arrive and pass status, so completion is announced once.
- Don’t: Wrap the text in a live region; a screen reader would read every token aloud.
- Do: Pass a stable renderCitation, built once at module scope or with useMemo.
- Don’t: Create the renderer inline on every render; finished blocks then render again on every token.

### Content

- Override doneAnnouncement only with a short, complete sentence: “Summary complete.”

## API

### `Caret` (component)

`className`, `ref`, `id` and the other DOM props go to `<span data-slot="caret">`.

### `StreamingText` (component)

Text that arrives a token at a time.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` (required) | `string` |  | Everything received so far. Grows; never rewritten from the top. |
| `doneAnnouncement` | `string` |  | Spoken once when a stream that was running completes. |
| `errorAnnouncement` | `string` |  | Spoken once when a stream that was running fails. |
| `messages` | `MessagesOverride<StreamingTextMessages>` |  | Words for translation: the default done and error announcements. Keys left out come from `MessagesProvider`, then English. |
| `renderCitation` | `((n: number) => ReactNode)` |  | How an inline `[n]` marker renders. Without it the marker stays as text. Pass a stable function (module scope or `useCallback`): finished blocks skip re-rendering only while it stays the same. |
| `status` | `StreamStatus` | `done` | Where the stream is. `streaming` shows the caret and sets `aria-busy`; the move from `streaming` to `done` or `error` is announced once. Defaults to `done`. |
| `tone` (deprecated) | `"default" \| "muted"` |  | Deprecated: Since 0.7.0; removed in 1.0.0. Use `variant`, which takes the same values: a muted ink is a presentation, and `tone` is a status. |
| `variant` | `"default" \| "muted"` |  | `muted` for text the reader may skim — reasoning, not the answer. |

`className`, `ref`, `id` and the other DOM props go to `<div data-slot="streaming-text">`.

## Accessibility

Nothing in it takes focus, so there is no keyboard table.

### Mola handles

- The text is `aria-busy` while it streams, so it is not read token by token.
- A polite status says “Response complete.” or “Response stopped with an error.” once, when a running stream ends, and not on mount; inside an `AgentRun` the run announces the outcome instead.
- The caret is hidden from screen readers, and under reduced motion it stops blinking.

### You handle

- Set `doneAnnouncement` when “Response complete.” is not the right words for what finished.
- Name the citations you render through `renderCitation`; `Citation` does this from the source’s title.

### Testing status

- Automated, jsdom: each of its 6 stories is rendered and checked with axe on every pull request.
- Automated, browser: every story is checked in Chromium with axe, colour contrast included, in both themes, and for overflow at 390px.
- Keyboard in unit tests: not applicable.
- Screen readers: not yet tested by hand.
